messages.subject: IRT Poisson model
parts:
Hi all,

I have been trying to implemente the following model (a particular model of that presented in https://cdr.lib.unc.edu/downloads/xd07gt356, Equation 3, when pij=1):

Y_{ij} ~ Poisson(lambda_{ij})
lambda_{ij} = exp(a_i(theta_j-b_i))

where theta_j, a_i, b_i play, essentially, the same role as in the 2PL usual model (for binary response). Then, I have written the following code:

_______________________________________________________________________________________
name <- 'C2PLPoi'
par <- c(a = .5, b = -2)
est <- c(TRUE, TRUE)
P.C2PLPoi <- function(par,Theta,ncat=Inf,itemdata){
  a <- par[1]
  b <- par[2]
  y<-itemdata
  lambda <- exp(a*(Theta-b))
  P <- dpois(y,lambda)
  P
}

mC2PLPoi<-createItem(name, par=par, est=est,
                     P=P.C2PLPoi)

a<- abs(rnorm(10))
b <- rnorm(10)
theta <- rnorm(500)
mlambda<-matrix(exp(a*(theta-b)),500,10)
mY <- matrix(0,500,10)
for(r in 1:10){
mY[,r] <- rpois(n=500,lambda=mlambda[,r])
}

_______________________________________________________________________________________

Then, I have execetude the above code, in two different ways, with the respective message errors also presented:

1)
mirt(mY, 1, 'mC2PLPoi', customItems=list(mC2PLPoi=mC2PLPoi))


"I1" re-mapped to ensure all categories have a distance of 1 "I2" re-mapped to ensure all categories have a distance of 1 "I3" re-mapped to ensure all categories have a distance of 1 "I4" re-mapped to ensure all categories have a distance of 1 "I5" re-mapped to ensure all categories have a distance of 1 "I6" re-mapped to ensure all categories have a distance of 1 "I7" re-mapped to ensure all categories have a distance of 1 "I8" re-mapped to ensure all categories have a distance of 1 "I9" re-mapped to ensure all categories have a distance of 1 "I10" re-mapped to ensure all categories have a distance of 1 Error in dpois(y, lambda) : Non numeric argument for a mathematical function In addition: Warning message: The following items have a large number of categories which may cause estimation issues: 2 4 8 9 10

_______________________________________________________________________________________

2)
mY <- remap.distance(mY)
mirt(mY, 1, 'mC2PLPoi', customItems=list(mC2PLPoi=mC2PLPoi))

Error in dpois(y, lambda) : Non numeric argument for a mathematical function In addition: Warning message: The following items have a large number of categories which may cause estimation issues: 2 4 8 9 10
_______________________________________________________________________________________

I Think that, essentially, those issues are due that the model has an "infinite number of categories" and, the, it is not possible to implement through mirt.

Any help is welcome,

Best,

Caio

messages.author: b330c2028fed415b
messages.subject: Re: IRT Poisson model
parts:
Hi Caio,

I'm afraid count data is not easily supported by this function, as the table of expected counts is positively unbounded; hence, the expectation tables would need to account for each unique count in the complete dataset, which makes the E-table quite massive. There is, however, the countirt package to perform such analyses (https://github.com/mbsmn/countirt), which you may find helpful. It's possible that I'll add count IRT models to mirt in the future, but this is low on my TODO list. Cheers.

Phil
